caption: The drawing depicts a single wall-mounted lantern with a glass and metal construction, shown against a plain, light-colored background. The lantern has a trapezoidal shape, tapering downwards, and is topped with a reddish-brown, four-sided roof that curves slightly outward and comes to a point, where a small blue-gray finial is present. The body of the lantern consists of four transparent glass panels framed with metallic-looking strips in a pale blue-gray color. Inside the lantern, at the base, there is a brass or golden-brown circular lamp. The lantern door is outlined, featuring a small circular ring handle on the front panel. On the right side, a greenish metal bracket is depicted, which is used for mounting the lantern to a wall. At the bottom of the lantern, there is a small, spherical metallic finial. The composition is centered on the page, and there are no background elements other than the solid color. At the bottom right, the name "Leslie J. Maskim" and the numbers "Del.1390-1" are inscribed.
title: Bracket Lamp
